## CameraArm

`res://assets/scripts/camera/CameraArm.gd`, extends [`Node3D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node3d.html)

Holds a VirtualCamera out from a pawn, following a look direction, and pulls it in so walls don't come between camera and pawn.

It's Unreal's spring arm, as a plain node. The PlayerController owns one arm per player and moves it to each pawn it takes (see CameraMount); a pawn's scene may also place its own.

It's idle unless it's active, which is when a player is looking through it. An idle arm does no work and reads nothing, and it never reads input itself: PlayerController tells it where to look. So AI or a cutscene could drive it just the same.

Its one collision check each frame is a physics query outside the physics step. That's safe with Godot's default setting, where physics doesn't run on its own thread. A project that turns that on would have to move this.

### Settings and properties

- `preset: CameraPreset`: The settings. Empty means the defaults.

### Functions

- `apply_preset(new_preset: CameraPreset) -> void`: Takes these settings (or the defaults, for null) now: the arm's place, length, pitch, field of view and collision radius. For an arm moving to another pawn, whose preset may differ.
- `get_view() -> VirtualCamera`: The view on the end of the arm.
- `ignore_body(body: CollisionObject3D) -> void`: Stops this body pulling the camera in, normally the pawn holding the arm.
- `clear_ignored() -> void`: Forgets every ignored body, for an arm moving to another pawn.
- `set_active(active: bool) -> void`: Starts or stops the arm's work. Only the arm a player is looking through needs to run.
- `set_look(new_yaw: float, new_pitch: float) -> float`: Where to look, as a yaw and pitch in radians. Pitch is limited to the preset's range, and the result is returned.
- `get_pitch() -> float`
- `zoom(steps: float) -> void`: Changes the arm's length by this many steps. Positive is further out.
- `get_length() -> float`
- `get_current_length() -> float`: How long the arm actually is right now, after walls.
- `_how_far_out() -> float`: Casts the camera's sphere out along the arm, and returns how far it gets.

## CameraMount

`res://assets/scripts/camera/CameraMount.gd`, extends [`Node3D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node3d.html)

Where a player's camera arm attaches to a pawn, and with what settings.

One camera per player, owned by the PlayerController (pawn spec 8.18). A CameraMount is a plain marker a pawn's scene places under its Visual node. It does nothing itself: the PlayerController moves its one arm here when it takes the pawn, and applies this preset.

A pawn without one gets the arm on its Visual node, with the default settings (CameraPreset's). A pawn whose scene places its own CameraArm, or a VirtualCamera of its own (at the eyes, say), uses that instead, and no mount is needed.

How to use it: add a CameraMount under the pawn scene's Visual node, and give it a CameraPreset (arm length, height, field of view). Its position is ignored: the preset's mount_height and shoulder_offset place the arm. The static functions find a pawn's camera pieces:

```gdscript
CameraMount.arm_of(pawn)      # its arm, or null
CameraMount.view_of(pawn)     # the view a camera attaches to
```

### Settings and properties

- `preset: CameraPreset`: The arm's settings for this pawn. Empty means the defaults.

### Functions

- `mount_of(pawn: Pawn) -> Node3D` *(static)*: Where a player's arm attaches on this pawn: the CameraMount under its Visual if the scene has one, else its Visual itself.
- `preset_of(pawn: Pawn) -> CameraPreset` *(static)*: The arm's settings for this pawn: its CameraMount's preset, or null for the defaults.
- `arm_of(pawn: Pawn) -> CameraArm` *(static)*: This pawn's arm, or null: one placed in its scene, or the player's while they have it. Looked for on its Visual and its mount.
- `view_of(pawn: Pawn) -> VirtualCamera` *(static)*: The view a camera should attach to when this pawn is possessed: its arm's, or else the first VirtualCamera in its scene, or null.

## CameraPreset

`res://assets/scripts/camera/CameraPreset.gd`, extends [`Resource`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_resource.html)

The settings for a CameraArm, as a resource a designer can make and share.

A pawn type with its own feel gets its own preset (on its CameraMount). With none, a pawn uses these defaults, a third-person orbit. An arm length of 0 is first person.

### Settings and properties

- `arm_length: float` = `6.0`: How long the arm starts, in metres.
- `min_length: float` = `1.5`
- `max_length: float` = `16.0`
- `zoom_step: float` = `0.75`: How much one step of the mouse wheel changes the length.
- `mount_height: float` = `1.5`: Where the arm starts, above the pawn's feet.
- `shoulder_offset: float` = `0.0`: Sideways, for an over-the-shoulder view. Positive is to the right.
- `start_pitch: float` = `-20.0`: How the view starts, in degrees. Negative is looking down.
- `min_pitch: float` = `-70.0`
- `max_pitch: float` = `50.0`
- `fov: float` = `75.0`: The field of view, in degrees.
- `collision_radius: float` = `0.2`: How thick the camera counts as when it's pulled in by walls, in metres.
- `collision_mask: int` = `1`: What the camera can't pass through. By default only the ground's layer, so that pawns don't shove the camera around.
- `return_speed: float` = `8.0`: How fast the camera moves back out after a wall or hill has pulled it in, in metres per second. It pulls in at once, so it never goes through anything, and comes back gently, so it doesn't snap around.

## FreeFlyCamera

`res://assets/scripts/camera/FreeFlyCamera.gd`, extends [`Node3D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node3d.html)

A camera that flies freely, for a player with no pawn: the spectator.

For the spectator view between matches, while waiting to respawn, or after letting go of a pawn. PossessionCoordinator.spectate() starts it: the PlayerController makes one the first time and flies it with the player's keys and mouse.

It isn't a Pawn. A Pawn is a whole character: it's simulated on ticks, rolled back, networked, recorded in replays, counted on a team, seen by the AI and killed by the kill floor. A spectator needs none of that. Unreal does the same: its PlayerController spawns its spectator on its own machine only, and nothing else in the game knows it's there. So it's local and per rendered frame, like the camera arm: never ticked, never sent over the network, never rolled back.

What it carries:
- View: a VirtualCamera, which the PlayerController's real camera follows while spectating.
- StreamingSource: keeps the world loaded around it while it's flying (`keeps_world_loaded`), so flying away from every pawn still shows ground. On a client it loads only that client's world, as any camera's source does.

How to use it: nothing to set up for the default. A game wanting different settings or a model for its spectator makes a scene whose root is a FreeFlyCamera and sets it as the PlayerController's spectator_scene.

Controls (read by the PlayerController): WASD flies where the view looks, Space and Ctrl go straight up and down (the jump and crouch keys, the PlayerController's fly_up_key and fly_down_key), and the mouse looks. 10 m/s, 25 with the sprint key held, and with it held the wheel ramps that fast speed up or down, up to 75. The wheel on its own zooms, by narrowing the field of view as a lens does, so it stays where it is; the mouse turns slower to match. The middle mouse button (middleMouse_button) resets the zoom.

It goes through ground and walls: there's no collision.

### Settings and properties

- `speed: float` = `10.0`: How fast it flies, in metres per second.
- `fast_speed: float` = `25.0`: How fast it flies with the sprint key held, in metres per second, to start with. The wheel changes it while sprint is held.
- `max_fast_speed: float` = `75.0`: The most the wheel can raise the fast speed to, in metres per second. The least is speed.
- `fast_speed_step: float` = `5.0`: How much one notch of the wheel changes the fast speed, in metres per second.
- `zoom_per_notch: float` = `1.25`: How much one notch of the wheel zooms in or out, as a multiple: 1.25 makes things look 1.25 times bigger.
- `max_zoom: float` = `8.0`: The most it zooms in, as a multiple of how big things look at fov.
- `seconds_to_full_speed: float` = `0.15`: How long it takes to reach full speed from standing, or to stop, in seconds. 0 is at once.
- `fov: float` = `75.0`: The field of view while it's the view, in degrees.
- `keeps_world_loaded: bool` = `true`: On: it keeps the world loaded around it while it's flying, through its StreamingSource. It can be changed while flying (the mass battle turns it off, so its own sources decide what's loaded). GDScript note: set(value) runs whenever the value is assigned, so the source follows at once.
- `view: VirtualCamera` = `null`: Where the real camera goes. Made here if the scene doesn't have one called View.
- `streaming_source: StreamingSource` = `null`: The source that keeps the world loaded around it. Made here if the scene doesn't have one called StreamingSource.

### Functions

- `get_zoom() -> float`: How zoomed in it is: 1 is none, 2 makes things look twice as big.
- `change_zoom(notches: float) -> void`: Zooms by this many notches of the wheel (in is positive), between none and max_zoom.
- `get_fast_speed() -> float`: The fast speed now, in metres per second: fast_speed, as the wheel has changed it.
- `change_fast_speed(notches: float) -> void`: Changes the fast speed by this many notches of the wheel (up is positive), between speed and max_fast_speed.
- `begin(at: Vector3) -> void`: Starts flying from this place, standing still. The PlayerController passes where its camera is, so the view doesn't jump.
- `end() -> void`: Stops flying. It stays where it is, and no longer keeps the world loaded.
- `is_flying() -> bool`: True between begin() and end().
- `teleport(to: Vector3) -> void`: Jumps to this place and stops there, as for an overview point. Which way it faces is the player's look, which the PlayerController sets (PlayerController.place_spectator()).
- `reset_zoom() -> void`: Back to no zoom (the middle mouse button).
- `fly(wish: Vector3, fast: bool, yaw: float, pitch: float, delta: float) -> void`: Moves it for one rendered frame. wish: x to the right, y up, z backward, each from -1 to 1, the way the keys give them. yaw and pitch are the player's look, in radians, and the view faces that way.

## PlayerCamera

`res://assets/scripts/camera/PlayerCamera.gd`, extends [`Camera3D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_camera3d.html)

The one real camera, which follows a VirtualCamera. PlayerController owns it.

It only follows a view; possession and the 3D cursor live elsewhere. It copies the view's position every rendered frame instead of being reparented onto it. So a pawn being freed can't take the camera with it, and if the view disappears, the camera just holds where it was.

It leaves the scene's own camera alone until it's given a view.

### Functions

- `set_view(view: VirtualCamera) -> void`: Starts following a view. Null stops following, and the camera holds where it is.
- `get_view() -> VirtualCamera`

## VirtualCamera

`res://assets/scripts/camera/VirtualCamera.gd`, extends [`Node3D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node3d.html)

A place for the real camera to be.

Put one where the view should be, such as on a CameraArm or at a pawn's eyes, and PlayerCamera follows it. It does nothing itself, so having one costs nothing.

### Settings and properties

- `fov: float` = `75.0`: The field of view while the camera is here, in degrees.
